company_verdict: Right brand, wrong door, wrong year. Quantiphi is Mumbai-headquartered AI/analytics consulting — exactly the industry Omkar is aiming at — but I re-verified its Workday board live today and the India side is a mid-to-senior experienced-hire wall: 108 of 110 global postings are FTE, the single Intern req on the entire planet is "Intern - IT & Facilities Support" in Boston (JR10760), and searchText for graduate, campus and fresher all return zero. Of ~50 India reqs, exactly one (PMO Analyst, JR11629) has a stated floor under 2 years, and every other one starts at 3+ with a median of 4-7. He should spend one evening on this portal, not one week: submit Resume Dropbox (JR467), get a Mumbai employee to flag it, and put the real effort into the DJSCE placement cell, because off-portal campus hiring is the only channel where a May-2027 graduand is actually the target audience.
best_channel: Campus placement via the DJSCE TPO — with a referral-flagged Resume Dropbox (JR467) submission as the backstop. Justification: the portal channel is structurally closed to him, and I confirmed that rather than assumed it (intern facet = 1 req, US facilities only; graduate/campus/fresher = 0 hits; the two "entry level" text matches resolve to that same Boston intern posting). Nothing on the board is addressed to a student. Meanwhile Quantiphi's India delivery centres are in Mumbai (Eureka, Quantum and ISD sites all appear as location tags) and DJSCE is a top-tier Mumbai engineering college, so an off-portal campus/pre-placement track is plausible — but it is unverifiable from the feed and must be checked with the TPO directly. Do NOT treat an ordinary experienced-hire application as the channel here; it is the lowest-yield of the three.
may_2027_fit: His graduation date disqualifies him from Quantiphi's entire posted India board on channel alone, before qualifications even get examined. Every India req is workerSubType=FTE, full time, experienced hire, written for someone who can start now — and most of my picks were posted between April and September 2026, so they will be closed long before June 2027. There is no India internship, trainee, graduate or analyst programme to slot a Jan-May 2027 final semester into; that is a verified negative, not a hole in the search. The asymmetry this creates is actually useful: because JR467 (Resume Dropbox) carries no requisition, no years bar and no skill list, it is the one place he can state dual availability — "Jan-May 2027 final-semester internship, Mumbai on-site, full-time from June 2027" — and have a recruiter match him against an intern or trainee need that never gets posted publicly. Every application he makes here should carry that exact two-line availability statement in the first paragraph, because his timing is the first thing that will disqualify him and the only thing he can pre-empt.

picks.title: Resume Dropbox
picks.location: IN MH Mumbai Eureka (primary) + IN KA Bengaluru + IN KL Trivandrum + Canada Remote + USA Remote — confirmed live today, 5 locations
picks.years_bar: none stated — the only India posting with no experience requirement at all
picks.why_fit: The complete posted requirement is one sentence: 'If "No Matching Jobs" are found, please submit your resume/ cover letter in word or PDF format so that the Talent team of Quantiphi will review and take necessary action.' There is no years bar, no degree line, no skill list — so he satisfies 100% of the written qualifications, which is true of exactly ONE of ~50 India postings. Primary location IN MH Mumbai Eureka matches his Mumbai base, and I re-confirmed today that it is still live across all five locations. Score is capped at 55 not because he fails anything but because a posting with no qualifications produces no qualification match to reward — it is a queue, not a req.
picks.gaps: None posted, which is precisely the problem. JR467 has been live since 2023-04-12 with no end date and no requisition attached, so it drains into an unmonitored talent-team queue with no hiring manager waiting on it. Unreferred, realistic conversion is close to zero. Do not mistake 'I meet every stated requirement' for 'I am in contention.'
picks.learnable_edge: None needed to submit — this is a packaging problem, not a skills problem. Front-load the one-page summary with the exact phrases Quantiphi's own India reqs repeat: 'Advanced SQL' and 'Power BI' (named verbatim together in the Data Analysis bullet of JR11666 and JR11742 — he has both outright), and 'RAG systems, vector databases, prompt engineering, multi-agent' (named in JR11938 and JR11910-1 — KOP AI and LawzyAI are direct evidence). Put the dual availability line above the fold.
picks.referral_leverage: high — worthless without one, decisive with one. Quantiphi's Engagement Manager JD (JR11266) lists as a core responsibility 'Work closely with talent acquisition and resource management teams to identify, vet, and onboard suitable candidates (BAs, Senior BAs, Developers, Architects etc.) for project roles across Geographies', meaning Mumbai delivery managers are formally chartered to source candidates themselves and can pull a dropbox entry out of the queue rather than merely co-signing a portal application.
picks.timing: Submit now, September 2026. State verbatim in the first line of the cover letter: 'Available immediately for a January-May 2027 full-time final-semester internship, Mumbai on-site; available for full-time employment from June 2027.' The dual availability is the entire reason to use a queue with no req attached — it is the only Quantiphi entry point flexible enough to be matched against an unposted intern or trainee need.

picks.title: PMO Analyst
picks.location: Workday location tag: IN KA Bengaluru ONLY (I re-confirmed this today — the facet returns Bengaluru and nothing else). The JD body text says 'Location - Bangalore/Mumbai'. Confirm a Mumbai base before investing.
picks.years_bar: 1-3 (header 'Experience - 1 to 3 Years'); must-have bullet says '1-2 years'
picks.why_fit: Highest genuine qualification overlap on the board, because the must-have list is almost entirely non-technical. 'Proficiency in Google Suite (Sheets, Doc, PowerPoint)' — he has this plus strong Excel and PowerBI; no SQL, Python, Java or C++ is demanded anywhere in this posting. 'Ability to manage multiple tasks simultaneously and prioritize effectively in a fast-paced environment' and 'Strong organizational skills with meticulous attention to detail' — Vice Chairperson of Trinity plus Head of Marketing at DJS S4DS held concurrently with 10+ commercial freelance projects. 'Excellent written and verbal communication skills. Ability to communicate clearly and concisely with diverse stakeholders' — at Infiheal he owned Series A investor materials end-to-end and engaged Brazilian and Saudi government bodies, which is diverse stakeholder communication by any reading. 'Proactive and problem-solving mindset' + 'Demonstrated ability to work independently and as part of a team' — shipped a registration platform for 10,000+ users in 8 days. Good-to-have 'Looker Dashboard Management: Utilize and maintain Looker dashboards to visualize resource data, identify trends, and provide actionable insights to stakeholders' — his funnel drop-off tracking on that 10,000-user platform and his competition EDA work are the same analytical shape in a different tool. The role itself (resource allocation, utilisation reporting, staffing-gap flagging) sits squarely inside his stated 'product operations' target.
picks.gaps: One must-have he genuinely misses: '1-2 years of experience in a coordination, administrative, or project support role within a professional services or project-driven environment.' He has ~13 months of internships, but none inside a professional-services or consulting delivery org — the Infiheal Founder's Office role is the closest honest analogue and it is an early-stage startup, not professional services. Do not let him overstate this. Also missing outright: Google Looker Studio, which is named in the 'Tools Used' line AND in the good-to-have block; and Workday, named in both 'Tools Used' and 'Familiarity with WorkDay - Processes, Reports'. He has never touched Workday. Finally, the Workday location facet says Bengaluru only despite the JD text — a Mumbai-based candidate may be a location mismatch regardless of qualifications.
picks.learnable_edge: Google Looker Studio — free, no licence, no heavy language, credibly learnable in 2-3 weeks, and it is the single highest-yield item on this entire posting because it is named TWICE (in 'Tools Used' and in 'Proficiency in using and creating dashboards within Looker'). Concrete deliverable: rebuild his existing funnel drop-off tracking from the 10,000-user registration platform as a public Looker Studio dashboard, plus one mock resource-utilisation/staffing-gap dashboard, and put both links on the resume — that turns the most specific good-to-have bullet into a clickable artefact. Second, 'Basic understanding of project management methodologies (e.g., Agile, Waterfall)' — one weekend on a free Agile/Scrum primer covers a literal good-to-have bullet. Workday is NOT learnable: no free tier, certification is partner-gated, no self-study route. He must not claim it.
picks.referral_leverage: high — a referrer converts this from a rejected experienced-hire application into the right conversation. The ask a referrer should make is NOT 'consider him for JR11629'; it is 'the PMO function is actively hiring at the junior end — is there a PMO/resource-management intern seat in Mumbai for Jan-May 2027?' JR11629 is the evidence that the function exists and is short-staffed. Target a PMO or resource-management lead, or any Engagement Manager (per the JR11266 sourcing charter).
picks.timing: Full-time FTE req posted 2026-08-10, already 30+ days old, wanting a current joiner — it will be filled well before he is free, so treat a cold application as a lottery ticket, not a plan. Declare: 'Available January-May 2027 for a full-time final-semester internship; full-time from June 2027.' Realistically this is a Q4 2026 referral conversation aimed at a Jan-2027 internship start, using this req as the door-opener.

picks.title: Senior Business Analyst - Conversational AI (Conversation Designer, Delivery)
picks.years_bar: 3 to 6 years — hard floor, not met
picks.why_fit: Worth knowing about because it has the shortest required-skills list of any Mumbai BA role — four bullets — and he clears three of them on paper. Required bullet 1, 'Experience in at least one of the following areas: Analytics, Conversational AI, Linguistics, Copywriting, UX Design or Product Design', is an OR across six fields and he satisfies it twice: Analytics (CypherSOL transaction-category and entity-recognition models; Analytrix'26 Datathon win; Datazen Spotify EDA win) and Conversational AI (KOP AI's 10 stateful LLM agents; LawzyAI's LLM query normalisation). Required bullet 4, 'Excellent aptitude in business analysis and awareness of quantitative analysis techniques. Your plans and actions are backed by not just gut feeling but also customer/ industry/ market research', is a near-restatement of the Bigul PM internship (competitor benchmarking of trading apps, feature-gap analysis) and the Spotify win (reframed India strategy from growth to monetisation/margin off large-scale EDA). Required bullet 2, 'Excellent communication, articulation, abstraction, analytical and presentation skills' — 4th of 400+ at IIT Bombay Ace The Case, 13 podium finishes, Series A deck ownership. The nice-to-have 'Strong understanding of the NLP space (natural language understanding, sentiment analysis, personality insight, Generative AI etc.), conversational interfaces, and leveraging existing services and libraries (integration, configuration, training, continuous learning)' is where he is unusually strong for his level: KOP AI (RAG over PDFs/YouTube with page and timestamp citations, ChromaDB, Groq, Llama 3.1) and LawzyAI (TF-IDF retrieval fed by LLM normalisation).
picks.gaps: 'Experience: 3 to 6 years' is an explicit floor and he has ~13 months of internships plus freelance. Qualification bullets are ANDed, so this is a NO today — not a stretch, and no amount of project strength converts it. He also has zero hands-on with any named bot platform (DialogFlow/API.AI, Cloud ML, Microsoft Bot Framework, Azure Cognitive Services, Amazon Lex, IBM Watson, Wit.ai, Salesforce Einstein), no voice processing (text-to-speech, speech-to-text), and no PMP or PSM certification.
picks.learnable_edge: Google Dialogflow CX — free trial tier, no Java or C++, a working demo bot inside 2-3 weeks. It is the FIRST platform named in the nice-to-have block, so one shipped bot converts the strongest preferred bullet from an absence into a demo link. Bolt on a free text-to-speech/speech-to-text leg for one more weekend to cover 'Well versed with voiced based processing'. Neither touches the 3-year floor — do this because it makes him the obvious internal candidate when this practice opens a junior seat, not because it makes him applicable now.
picks.referral_leverage: medium-high — the application is dead on the years bar, so a referrer is the ONLY mechanism here. The valuable ask is to reach someone in the conversational-AI delivery practice and pitch a Jan-May 2027 internship against this team's workload, showing the Dialogflow demo plus KOP AI.
picks.timing: Posted 2026-04-28 and now five months stale — do not apply cold. Use it as a mid-2027 target and a referral conversation starter. Declared availability if the conversation opens: 'Jan-May 2027 final-semester internship; full-time from June 2027.'

picks.title: Senior Business Analyst
picks.years_bar: 3+ in the requirements bullet; header says 4-7 — contradictory, and he clears neither
picks.why_fit: The best title-to-target match in Mumbai, and the degree line is unusually generous: 'Bachelor's Degree in Advanced degree in Business (CA/MBA/CFA), Economics or Engineering' — B.Tech CSE clears it outright with no MBA required, which is rarer than it sounds for a BA req. 'Experience in relevant technology domain (for example, AI/ML, Business Intelligence and Data Analytics) (strongly desired)' — B.Tech CSE with a Data Science specialisation at 8.82 CGPA, plus CypherSOL ML work and PowerBI. 'Excellent written and verbal communication skills with the ability to convey complex information in a clear, concise manner and deliver presentations to diverse audiences' — owned the Infiheal Series A pitch deck, fundraise narrative and investor presentations end-to-end and contributed to closing co-investors. 'Experience with elicitation of business requirements, leading communication with internal and external stakeholders, analysing problem statements and drawing up solutions for possible implementation' — the Bigul PM internship (feature-gap analysis, UX friction reduction on algo workflows) and the Infiheal IndiGo/HDFC Bank pipeline from first contact to proposal. 'Proficient in Google Workspace and MS Office Suite (Word, Excel, PowerPoint...)' — strong Excel.
picks.gaps: '3+ years of experience in decision support, business analysis, business consulting or project management' is a hard floor he does not meet with ~13 months of internships; the 4-7 header is worse still. Beyond years, four separate bullets are genuine misses: 'Customer facing migration experience, including service discovery, assessment, planning, execution, and operations' — he has never run a migration of any kind; 'Ability to serve as an advanced technical leader providing advice, counsel, and analysis on business intelligence and AI/ML issues' — that is a seniority claim he cannot support; 'In-depth knowledge of business intelligence functions, advanced analytics, industry standards and best practices'; and MS Access, named explicitly in the proficiency bullet, which he does not have. Plus the role's insurance domain, which he has no exposure to.
picks.learnable_edge: MS Access basics — one weekend, included with Microsoft 365, and it is the single named tool in the proficiency bullet he is missing; building one small relational DB with forms and queries makes that bullet honest. Requirements-artefact fluency (BRD, user stories, requirement traceability matrix) — 1-2 weeks: the JD names exactly these artefacts, and he can produce a real BRD and RTM retroactively for LawzyAI and attach them, which is far more convincing than a certificate. Be clear-eyed: neither of these moves the 3-year floor, and nothing learnable does.
picks.referral_leverage: medium — a referral cannot manufacture three years of experience, and the migration-experience and technical-leadership bullets are seniority markers a referrer cannot vouch past. Its use is as a named destination: 'this is the role I am building toward' in a conversation with a Mumbai Senior BA or Engagement Manager.
picks.timing: Posted 2026-05-20, four months stale, experienced-hire FTE. Not applicable now. Target it for a June-2027-onward start only after a year of full-time work elsewhere, or cite it in a referral conversation as the trajectory he is aiming at.

picks.title: Senior Machine Learning Engineer (GenAI / agentic, GCP)
picks.location: IN MH Mumbai Eureka — Mumbai-only, the cleanest location match on the board
picks.years_bar: 3-6 years of hands-on ML engineering — hard floor, not met
picks.why_fit: Included for one reason: the highest raw wording-to-resume match of any posting on this board, which makes it his single best referral artefact even though he cannot apply. The bar is only five lines, and the last one — 'Experience building GenAI, traditional ML, and computer vision applications; MLOps practices; retrieval-augmented generation' — he can evidence clause by clause: GenAI and RAG via KOP AI (10 stateful LLM agents orchestrated in parallel, RAG over PDFs and YouTube with page and timestamp citations, ChromaDB, Groq, Llama 3.1) and LawzyAI (LLM query normalisation feeding TF-IDF retrieval); traditional ML via CypherSOL (transaction-category and entity-recognition models replacing rule-based analytics) and the ML Quest fake-job-posting classifier win; computer vision via LearnSphere (ONNX FER+, OpenCV, per-user SVM correcting domain bias). 'Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Engineering, Mathematics, or related field' — clears outright. 'Expert-level Python proficiency with strong software engineering fundamentals: API design, testing, containerization' — FastAPI across LawzyAI and KOP AI, Docker, and a hand-rolled HTTP/1.1 server over raw TCP sockets in GitLane. The responsibilities also name multi-agent orchestration, prompt engineering, context optimization and hybrid retrieval combining vector embeddings with keyword search, which is KOP AI and LawzyAI described almost literally.
picks.gaps: '3-6 years of hands-on ML engineering' — hard floor, not met, and it is one of only five lines so it carries proportionally more weight. 'Proven track record shipping production ML systems in cloud environments with GCP (Vertex AI, BigQuery, Cloud Run) or equivalent' — he has shipped to Vercel and Firebase, never to a managed ML platform; AWS Academy ML Foundations and Google Cloud GenAI Skills Boost are intro credentials and do not evidence production ML. Separately and importantly: this is an engineering title, and he has explicitly said he does not want core SDE-style work — flag that before he invests effort chasing an ML Engineer ladder he did not ask for.
picks.learnable_edge: Google Cloud Skills Boost paths for BigQuery and Vertex AI — 2-4 weeks, free tier, and they extend a credential he already holds rather than starting from zero. The cloud line says 'GCP (Vertex AI, BigQuery, Cloud Run) or equivalent', so deploying one KOP AI agent as a live Cloud Run endpoint converts 'no cloud deployment' into a URL he can send. Does not close the 3-year floor.
picks.referral_leverage: medium — as a job application, none; as ammunition, high. A referral message that says 'here is a live Mumbai req whose five qualification lines describe four projects I have already shipped' is far stronger than a generic student outreach, and it is the most credible opener he has for any Quantiphi conversation.
picks.timing: Posted 2026-09-07, fresh, and will close in weeks — not applicable at his stage. Value is entirely as evidence in outreach, not as a submission.

picks.title: Associate Client Solutions Partner (P&C Insurance Domain)
picks.location: IN MH Mumbai Eureka (JD: 'Hybrid (Mumbai or Bangalore or Trivandrum)')
picks.years_bar: header 'Years of Experience: 6 to 8'; the only number in the requirements block is 'a minimum of 2+ years' — contradictory, but both readings exceed him
picks.why_fit: Listed last and only because it is the most consulting-shaped role on the India board and he asked for strategy/consulting. The responsibilities — drafting client proposals and RFP responses, financial proposals and customer business cases, deal reviews, pipeline and funnel maintenance against quarterly growth targets — are the closest match on this entire board to what he actually did at Infiheal: Series A investor materials end-to-end, fundraise narrative, and an enterprise B2B pipeline with IndiGo and HDFC Bank from first contact to proposal. 'Demonstrable ability to professionally communicate, present and influence key stakeholders at all levels of an organization, including executive and C-level' — investor presentations that contributed to closing co-investors, plus engagement with Brazilian and Saudi government bodies. 'Experience forecasting and tracking sales lifecycle and metrics' — funnel drop-off tracking and automated re-engagement on the 10,000-user platform.
picks.gaps: Three explicit hard blockers, none of them soft: (1) 'a minimum of 2+ years of experience in the Data/Analytics and AI specializing in Insurance' plus 'Knowledge of Insurance/P&C/Broker industry business models and regulatory landscape' — zero insurance exposure; (2) 'Direct experience selling to clients in the US and India' — his B2B work is India-side startup selling only, no US clients; (3) 'Excellent organizational skills including maintenance of client selling activity in enterprise CRM systems' — no Salesforce or any CRM whatsoever. The '(must have)' tag sits on 'Demonstrable experience in technical sales and solutions based on customer needs, especially in the areas of cloud, data, and artificial intelligence' — he has the data/AI half and none of the enterprise technical-sales half. Also flag honestly that this is presales/GTM, adjacent to but not the same as the analytics/BI/product-ops target he stated.
picks.learnable_edge: Salesforce Trailhead 'Sales Cloud Basics' and 'Sales Rep' trails — free, 1-2 weeks, and they close the enterprise-CRM bullet literally. Two weekends reading P&C insurance fundamentals (lines of business, underwriting, claims lifecycle, broker/MGA economics) turns the domain bullet from a blank into a conversation. Neither fixes 'Direct experience selling to clients in the US and India' or the 6-8 year header — this stays a no.
picks.referral_leverage: low — the blockers are domain and tenure, which referrals do not override, and the 6-8 header means even a sympathetic referrer has nothing to argue with.
picks.timing: Posted 2026-07-31, experienced hire, not applicable. Only relevant if he decides he wants presales/GTM consulting rather than analytics, in which case it is a post-2028 target.

referral_strategy:
A referral at Quantiphi is not a nice-to-have, it is the mechanism — and there is a structural reason visible in their own job text, not just the usual advice. Quantiphi's Engagement Manager JD (JR11266) lists as a core responsibility: "Work closely with talent acquisition and resource management teams to identify, vet, and onboard suitable candidates (BAs, Senior BAs, Developers, Architects etc.) for project roles across Geographies." Delivery-side managers there are formally chartered to source and vet candidates themselves, which means a referral from an Engagement Manager routes AROUND the portal rather than merely flagging a portal application. That is unusual and worth exploiting.

Who to approach, in priority order. (1) DJSCE alumni at Quantiphi Mumbai — LinkedIn people search with "Quantiphi" plus "Dwarkadas J. Sanghvi College of Engineering", filtered to Mumbai. Quantiphi runs three Mumbai sites (Eureka, Quantum, ISD all appear as location tags), so the alumni pool is real. Prioritise anyone titled Engagement Manager, Senior Business Analyst, or PMO/Resource Manager over ML engineers — those are the people attached to the reqs he can plausibly enter through. (2) The DJS S4DS and Trinity alumni networks — he is Head of Marketing at S4DS and Vice Chairperson of Trinity, which gives him a legitimate, non-cold reason to message seniors who have graduated into analytics consulting. (3) Quantiphi Mumbai talent-acquisition recruiters on LinkedIn, approached only AFTER the JR467 submission exists so the message has something concrete to point at.

What the ask should be — this matters more than who. Do NOT ask "can you refer me to JR11629", because every one of these reqs wants an immediate joiner and he is nine months away. Ask instead: "I have submitted to Resume Dropbox JR467. I graduate May 2027 and am free for a full-time final-semester internship January-May 2027 in Mumbai. Is there an intern or trainee seat on your team, or can you point my submission to whoever handles that?" Attach two artefacts: a Looker Studio dashboard link (because JR11629 names Looker Studio twice) and KOP AI (because JR11938's qualification lines read like its spec sheet). The unposted intern seat is the realistic prize here; the posted reqs are not.

One caveat so he does not over-invest: a referral raises his odds inside a pipeline that has no student lane at all. It cannot create one. That is why the DJSCE TPO check ranks above all of this.

skills_to_learn.skill: Google Looker Studio (dashboard building + connecting a data source)
skills_to_learn.why: Highest leverage item for Quantiphi specifically. Named TWICE on PMO Analyst (JR11629) — in the 'Tools Used : Google Sheets, Google Looker Studio, Google Docs, Google Slides, Workday' line and in the good-to-have 'Proficiency in using and creating dashboards within Looker' — and JR11629 is the single most realistic named opening on the whole India board. Also directly adjacent to the Looker/LookML ask in Senior Data Engineer - BI developer (JR10405-1). Unlocks 1 posting properly and softens a second, and his PowerBI experience transfers almost one-for-one.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free — Looker Studio itself is free with any Google account. Google's own 'Data Studio / Looker Studio' Skills Boost quest plus the official product tutorials. Deliverable, not just study: rebuild the funnel drop-off tracking from his 10,000-user registration platform as a public dashboard, plus one mock resource-utilisation dashboard, and put both URLs on the resume.

skills_to_learn.skill: JIRA + BPMN process modelling (draw.io is fine; Visio not required)
skills_to_learn.why: Named verbatim as the first TWO must-have bullets on both Healthcare BA reqs: 'Requirements Expertise: Elicitation, documentation, prioritization (JIRA, Azure DevOps)' and 'Process Modeling: Current/future state, optimization (BPMN, Visio)' — JR11666 (which lists Mumbai) and JR11742. Also universal BA currency across every firm he will apply to, so it never goes to waste. Cheapest effort-to-bullet ratio on this list.
skills_to_learn.resource: Free JIRA cloud tier (up to 10 users) — run one of his own freelance projects through a real board with epics and stories. BPMN via draw.io (free) using the official BPMN 2.0 quick-reference poster; model the CypherSOL bank-statement ingestion flow as current-state and future-state diagrams.

skills_to_learn.why: Named explicitly alongside a tool he already has, in the same bullet, on two reqs: 'Data Analysis: Advanced SQL, Data Visualization (Tableau, Power BI)' — JR11666 and JR11742. He has Advanced SQL and Power BI already, so Tableau is the only missing word in a bullet he otherwise fully satisfies. Its real value is market-wide: Tableau is on his stated gap list and appears across most BI/analyst postings in India.
skills_to_learn.resource: Tableau Public is free forever. Tableau's own free 'Get Started' video series, then rebuild one existing PowerBI dashboard in Tableau and publish to Tableau Public so the profile URL is linkable.

skills_to_learn.skill: AWS Cloud Practitioner + hands-on S3 and Redshift basics
skills_to_learn.why: Touches the largest number of Quantiphi postings of anything on this list. It closes the ONLY technical bullet he misses on Senior ML Engineer - Traditional (JR12055): 'AWS Data Ecosystem: Working knowledge of AWS S3 and Amazon Redshift for data ingestion, storage, and retrieval' — every other must-have on that req (Python/scikit-learn/Pandas/NumPy/Jupyter, model testing and evaluation, feature engineering and EDA, data preparation from multiple messy sources) he already has via CypherSOL. It also partially addresses JR9600, JR11248, JR11910-1, JR12057 and JR11771-1. Honest caveat: it closes a bullet, it does not close those reqs' 4+ year floors.
skills_to_learn.resource: AWS Skill Builder's free Cloud Practitioner Essentials course; exam ~USD 100. Free-tier hands-on: load a public CSV into S3, query it, and stand up a small Redshift Serverless workgroup within free-trial credits. Upgrades his AWS Academy ML Foundations certificate from intro to demonstrable.

skills_to_learn.skill: Google Dialogflow CX (build and ship one demo bot)
skills_to_learn.why: It is the FIRST platform named in the nice-to-have block of Senior BA - Conversational AI (JR9904), a Mumbai req whose four required bullets he otherwise largely satisfies: 'Experience in AI bot platforms, such as DialogFlow/API.AI, Cloud ML, Microsoft Bot Framework and Azure Cognitive Services, Amazon Lex, IBM Watson, Wit.ai, Salesforce Einstein etc.' One shipped bot converts the strongest preferred bullet on that posting from absent to demonstrable, and conversation design is a genuine BA-adjacent specialism rather than engineering.
skills_to_learn.resource: Google Cloud free trial credits plus the official Dialogflow CX quickstart and Skills Boost path. Build something tied to his own work — a bot front-end over LawzyAI's IPC/BNS lookup — so it doubles as portfolio rather than a throwaway tutorial.

skills_to_learn.skill: Time-series forecasting with Prophet, statsmodels and LightGBM
skills_to_learn.why: Closes the single largest must-have bullet on JR12057 (Mumbai listed): 'Build, evaluate, and tune statistical and ML-based forecasting models (ARIMA, LightGBM, Prophet, LSTMs/Transformers)' and 'Strong expertise in time-series forecasting and handling sequential data'. Also directly serves JR12055's 'specifically sales forecasting or growth prediction using time-series and tabular data'. All are free Python libraries layered on scikit-learn fluency he already has — no new language. Bonus: both of JR12057's good-to-haves he can already claim (retail/SKU work from the IES Business School runner-up; OpenCV computer vision from LearnSphere, which that JD names explicitly).
skills_to_learn.resource: Free: Prophet and statsmodels docs plus Rob Hyndman's 'Forecasting: Principles and Practice' (free online). Build one end-to-end retail demand-forecast project on a public Kaggle store-sales dataset, benchmarking ARIMA vs Prophet vs LightGBM with a written error analysis.

skills_to_learn.skill: LangChain / CrewAI (port existing KOP AI orchestration)
skills_to_learn.why: Named as a must-have on JR11910-1 ('Strong Python skills with ML libraries (scikit-learn, XGBoost, LightGBM) and agent frameworks (LangChain, CrewAI)') and on JR9600 ('Exposure on Agentic frameworks like langgraph and langchain'). He built 10-agent parallel orchestration by hand with ThreadPoolExecutor, which is arguably more impressive but reads as a miss against a framework-named bullet. Porting one workflow fixes the keyword gap cheaply. XGBoost and LightGBM in that same bullet are a one-afternoon addition to his scikit-learn fluency.
skills_to_learn.effort: 1 weekend for the port; 1 afternoon for XGBoost/LightGBM
skills_to_learn.resource: Free — LangChain and CrewAI docs and quickstarts. Frame it in interviews as a deliberate engineering choice ('I hand-rolled orchestration for latency control, 60-90s down to 8-12s; here is the same flow in LangChain'), which is a stronger story than either alone.

skills_to_learn.skill: GCP Vertex AI + BigQuery (Skills Boost paths)
skills_to_learn.why: The only gap besides years on JR11938, the Mumbai-only req whose five qualification lines match his portfolio most closely: 'Proven track record shipping production ML systems in cloud environments with GCP (Vertex AI, BigQuery, Cloud Run) or equivalent'. He already holds a Google Cloud GenAI Skills Boost credential, so this extends an existing credential rather than starting cold, and BigQuery SQL also feeds the Looker/BI track.
skills_to_learn.resource: Google Cloud Skills Boost (free monthly credits, frequent free-access promotions). Deploy one KOP AI agent to Cloud Run so 'shipped to a cloud environment' becomes a live URL rather than a claim.

skills_to_learn.skill: dbt Core + SQL window functions — market investment, NOT a Quantiphi key
skills_to_learn.why: Listing this ninth deliberately, as a correction. dbt is flagged as the 'highly recommended skill' on JR11771-1 and SQL window functions appear verbatim there and on JR12017, so it looks like a target. It is not: that same req also demands PySpark performance tuning, Apache Iceberg lakehouse design, EMR, Aurora PostgreSQL optimisation and roughly eighteen named AWS services. Learning dbt does NOT make JR11771-1 reachable. Learn it because it unlocks a whole class of analytics-engineering roles market-wide — and skip JR12017 entirely, where SnowPro Core closes one bullet out of nineteen.
skills_to_learn.resource: dbt Core is free and open source, SQL and YAML only — no Java or C++. Free dbt Fundamentals course on dbt Learn, run against DuckDB locally at zero cost. Window functions: Mode Analytics' free SQL tutorial.
